{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Jim Agler''' is a mathematician who is an emeritus professor at the [[University of California, San Diego]]. He is a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] since 2016, for "contributions to [[operator theory]] and the theory of [[analytic function]]s of [[Complex analysis|several complex variables]]".<ref name="ams">{{cite web|url=http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list|title=List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society|publisher=ams.org|accessdate=2016-05-22|archive-date=2018-08-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825194636/http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He obtained his Ph.D. from the [[Indiana University Bloomington]] in 1980 under the supervision of [[John B. Conway]].<ref name=":0">{{MathGenealogy|id=1789|title=Jim Agler}}</ref> His thesis was titled ''Subjordan Operators''.<ref name=":0" /> The thesis generalizes the notion of a [[Jordan operator]], originally studied by [[J. W. Helton]], which are of the form ''A + Q'' where <math>A^* = A, Q^2 = 0, AQ=QA</math> (defined on a [[Hilbert space]] over the complex numbers).<ref name=":1">{{Cite thesis|last=Agler|first=Jim|title=Subjordan Operators|date=August 1980|access-date=30 November 2025|publisher=Indiana University|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/302971200}}</ref> Restricting this operator to an [[invariant subspace]] produces a [[subjordan operator]]. All subjordan operators satisfy the equation <math>{T^*}^3 - 3{T^*}^2T + 3T^*T^2 - T^3 = 0</math> .<ref name=":1" /> The thesis also characterizes all subjordan operators in terms of the [[C* algebra]] <math>\mathbb{C}(I, M_2(\mathbb{C}))</math>.<ref name=":1" />

Agler and [[John McCarthy (mathematician) |John E. McCarthy]] are the authors of the book ''Pick Interpolation and Hilbert Function Spaces'' ([[American Mathematical Society]], 2002).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.euro-math-soc.eu/review/pick-interpolation-and-hilbert-function-spaces|title=Pick Interpolation and Hilbert Function Spaces &#124; European Mathematical Society}}</ref>

Some efforts to extend the [[Herglotz representation theorem]] are described in ''Classical function theory, Operator Dilation Theory, and Machine Computations on Multiply-Connected Domains''.<ref>Jim Agler, John Harland, and Benjamin J. Raphael (2008) ''Classical Function Theory, Operator Dilation Theory, and Machine Computations on Multiply-Connected Domains'', [[Memoirs of the American Mathematical Society]] #892, {{ISSN|0065-9266}}</ref>
